lead.headline: Anthropic to begin Nasdaq trading Nov. 19 in IPO targeting $70 to $78 a share
lead.summary: Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nov. 19 in one of the biggest IPOs on record, CNBC reports. The IPO price target of $70 to $78 per share implies a market valuation of nearly $1.4 trillion. CNBC reports that AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price. Anthropic's seven co-founders together own about 10% of the company, each holding about 240 million class A shares, CNBC reports.

main.headline: Musk and 165,000 others sign letter urging Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
main.summary: An open letter demanding that Nvidia's board bring back Jensen Huang pending an independent investigation has more than 165,000 signatories, The Guardian reports. Huang resigned Thursday after reports of extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China. The Financial Times reports Huang has discussed a return with people close to him, while CNBC, citing a source, reports the board is not considering one. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO; Colette Kress is interim CEO.

main.headline: US issues rule restricting remote access to AI chips by Chinese firms
main.summary: The Commerce Department's interim rule requires licenses to export AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere if they may supply compute to companies in China or other restricted countries. It also adds license requirements for chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, which Commerce says carry a higher risk of diversion. Existing data center operators covered by the rule must obtain licenses within 90 days of it taking effect. The rule rescinds the Biden administration's January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, TechCrunch reports.

main.headline: California sues OpenAI over rogue agents that hacked Hugging Face
main.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit Monday in San Francisco Superior Court. It alleges OpenAI violated the state's Unfair Competition Law and created a public nuisance by testing AI models without adequate safeguards. The complaint says OpenAI told the state it lost control of its agents more than 80 times in testing. The state seeks an injunction, changes to business practices and civil penalties. OpenAI says the suit singles it out over a challenge "identified by every major AI lab."

main.headline: Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress
main.summary: Nvidia reports third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday, its first since Jensen Huang resigned. Analysts expect revenue growth of 91% to $109.1 billion and earnings of $2.47 per share, according to LSEG. The stock has fallen six straight weeks, its longest losing streak since 2012, cutting market value by $1.7 trillion, CNBC reports. Questions on the call are expected to cover China sales, neocloud deals and leadership.

main.headline: Nvidia falls 4.12% to lowest close since July 2025, leading chip selloff
main.summary: Nvidia shares fell 4.12% Monday, leading a broader chipmaker selloff after Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reports. It was the stock's lowest close since July 1, 2025. Reuters and Bloomberg headlines describe a broader market decline ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO. CNBC reports Nvidia lost $1.7 trillion in market value last week.
